implementation_notes: TypeScript's structural typing accepts any string where an alias of string is expected, so the newtype is a type-level intersection with a phantom property keyed by a unique symbol: UserId and OrderId become mutually incompatible and nothing is emitted at runtime. Construction goes through a factory or a validating parse, and the cast back and forth is confined to that module. This is the compile-time equivalent of the classic wrapper at zero cost, but it protects only code that passes through the compiler.
pitfalls: as UserId is an unchecked assertion: any code that can write the cast bypasses the brand, so keep casts inside the factory and re-validate values that arrive from JSON.parse or the network.
Brands vanish in emitted JavaScript: untyped consumers, schema validators and dynamic configuration see a plain string, so the type must be paired with a runtime parse at the trust boundary.
Branded primitives still flow into Record<string, T>, Array<string> and spread/Object.keys results, where the brand is lost silently.

variants.name: class with private field and instanceof check
variants.idiom_name: class UserId with #private field and static parse
variants.implementation_notes: When the check must exist at runtime - untyped callers, plugin or DI boundaries, values rebuilt from configuration - the wrapper is a class with a #private field and a private constructor: the static factory is the only construction path and instanceof is a real check. It costs an allocation and needs explicit serialization, and it is the same object-shaped realization as in plain JavaScript.
pitfalls: instanceof breaks across duplicated module instances (dual-package hazard) and realms; add a Symbol.for-based brand or a structural check when the type crosses library boundaries.
Class instances are objects on the wire: JSON.stringify serializes only enumerable properties (private fields are invisible), so a toJSON or an explicit serializer is required.
Nominal classes lose assignability against the branded primitive form, so mixing both variants in one codebase creates conversion hotspots.
